author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:

  as a follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, on one page reached by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html renders a page listing every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it (owner-specified address).
Each veterinarian under a specialty is shown by full name, first name then last name, for example "Helen Leary".
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page; the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster.
A veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each of them (PRD Veterinarian directory edge case 3).
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it (edge case 4).
Every specialty renders on the one page; the page offers no paging, whatever the number of specialties.
The specialties, and the veterinarians under each, appear in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one (edge case 5).

The page carries the same navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory as every other page (REQ-SYS-001); that navigation gains no entry for the specialty directory, and no other page links to it.
The page's wording is hard-coded in no language and is present in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002).
The page offers no way to change a veterinarian or a specialty (NG-2).
non_goals: Any navigation entry or link from another page to the specialty directory; the owner left a visible entry point for a possible follow-up request (intake line 1).
Creating, editing, or deleting veterinarians or specialties; NG-2 is unchanged (intake line 1).
A machine-readable variant of the specialty directory; the owner asked for the HTML page only.
Searching or filtering specialties or veterinarians; the page takes no search input, so NG-9 holds.
Any change to the paged veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001).
notes: Boundary check: no contradiction. NG-2 unchanged per the quoted decision; NG-9 not implicated (a listing, not a search); REQ-SYS-001 and REQ-LANG-002 bind the new page as they bind every page. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. The page address is owner-specified in the intake request; the PRD keeps it out of prose and defers it to system-design.md#contracts. Narrowest readings taken per the owner's instruction, each recorded in PRD Open Questions: (1) no visible entry point until a follow-up request; (2) a specialty no veterinarian holds is listed with nothing under it, with no explicit 'none' marker. Ordering is left as 'stable' only, matching REQ-VET-001 edge case 1; the specific order is the designer's call. No prd-autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory stays inside the vet feature package (system-design.md Package Structure; ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization) and adds no new pattern, only two instances of in-force catalog patterns (architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog). (1) SpecialtyRepository: a read-only Repository<Specialty, Integer> that returns every specialty. It follows the PetTypeRepository lookup precedent and the VetRepository read-only base type. It is the only source that sees a specialty no veterinarian holds (edge case 4). (2) SpecialtyDirectory: an immutable Value object built by a static factory from the specialty list and the veterinarian collection. It owns the grouping and ordering rules, so VetController only loads, delegates, adds the result to the model, and selects the view (Web controller row; checklist: no business rule added to a controller). (3) VetController gains the GET /specialties.html handler rendering templates/vets/specialtyList.html through fragments/layout with an active-menu value that matches no existing nav entry. REQ-SYS-001 navigation therefore appears unchanged, with no link to the page. Ordering (edge case 5; designer's call per the prd-entry): specialties by name, veterinarians under each by last name then first name, id breaking remaining ties. Entries carry the specialty name and the holders' full names as first name, space, last name, so the value object holds strings, not mutable entities. Design-doc writes: vet package line, new Contracts rows for SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyDirectory, REQ-VET-003 joined to the Vet, Specialty, VetRepository and VetController rows, and the owner-specified address named on the VetController row, where the PRD defers it. No ADR: the order and placement belong to this slice alone and constrain no later one. Basis: grep and file reads of the vet package, PetTypeRepository and BaseEntity (no IDE oracle connected, so this is the weaker basis).
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html binds no request data: no @RequestParam, no @ModelAttribute, no form object, and no data binder for a persisted type. Binding target: none (security-principles.md Trust Boundaries, external input row; system-design.md Threat Model, mass-assignment row).

Double, SpecialtyDirectory unit tests (SpecialtyDirectoryTests): no boundary is crossed. Use real Vet and Specialty instances with ids set, as VetControllerTests.helen() already builds them (testing-principles.md Mocking Policy: never mock internal code).

Double, repository boundary for SpecialtyRepository in the VetControllerTests @WebMvcTest slice: a hand-written in-memory implementation registered through @TestConfiguration or @Import, whose specialty list each test sets (testing-principles.md Mocking Policy: hand-write mocks).

Double, repository boundary for VetRepository in VetControllerTests: the class's existing @MockitoBean stub, re-stubbed per test for findAll(). Framework-stub reason: the class-level @MockitoBean already owns the VetRepository bean and would shadow a hand-written one, and rewriting the existing tests is out of scope (testing-principles.md Mocking Policy: tolerated, not encouraged).

Framework transport: MockMvc, the one sanctioned harness (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy). Assert the view name and the SpecialtyDirectory model attribute, and assert the rendered names in the HTML where a test_name speaks to what the page shows.

Data source: VetController reads vets through the cached VetRepository.findAll() and specialties through SpecialtyRepository. Vet specialties are fetched eagerly, so the value object needs no open session (system-design.md Persistence: open-in-view disabled).

patterns.description: lookup-value repository precedent; SpecialtyRepository mirrors it but extends Repository, not JpaRepository, as VetRepository does
read-only Spring Data base type with @Transactional(readOnly = true) on the query method
layout fragment invocation, th:text-only rendering, and reuse of the existing vets, specialties and name message keys

risks.risk: BaseEntity does not override equals, and VetRepository.findAll() returns cached instances loaded apart from the SpecialtyRepository result. Object-equality matching would therefore silently list every specialty as unheld.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory matches a veterinarian's specialties to the listed specialties by id. A SpecialtyDirectoryTests case builds separate Specialty instances with equal ids to pin this (architecture-principles.md Domain Core: aggregates reference each other by identity).

risks.risk: Grouping or ordering written in the controller or template is a fresh Web controller violation, not covered by the recorded deviation.
risks.mitigation: All grouping and ordering live in SpecialtyDirectory. The template only iterates its entries (architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; Design Validation Checklist).

risks.risk: A write method on the new repository would open a mutation path the page must not have (NG-2).
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository extends Repository, not JpaRepository or CrudRepository, and declares only the read method (security-principles.md Trust Boundaries, privilege row: minimum scope).

risks.risk: Wording hard-coded in the template, or a new key added only to messages.properties, fails REQ-LANG-002 and I18nPropertiesSyncTest. The prd-entry file_targets name only the default bundle.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing vets, specialties and name keys where the wording fits. Add any new key to all eleven bundles listed in supporting_paths (system-design.md Contracts, REQ-LANG-002 paragraph).

risks.risk: Stored names are echoed into HTML.
risks.mitigation: Render only through th:text; never th:utext (system-design.md Threat Model, cross-site scripting row).

risks.risk: A mutable holder list, or entity references leaking out of the value object, breaks value-object immutability. The persistence-entity exception does not cover a type the framework does not instantiate.
risks.mitigation: Build SpecialtyDirectory as records holding strings, with List.copyOf for every list (architecture-principles.md Domain Core; Scoped exception, Does not cover row).

risks.risk: Vet-to-specialty links changed out of band do not appear until the vet cache clears.
risks.mitigation: Accepted. This is the existing behavior of the paged vet list, already tracked as Open Question 5 in system-design.md; no eviction change in this slice.

notes: The first dispatch-start for this dispatch (line 4) anchored to line 2 in error. Line 5 is the corrected dispatch-start anchored to the prd-entry at line 3. No design-doc-autofix records exist, so the autofix audit had nothing to check. The unpaged specialty set is a clinic-maintained lookup list, so the result size is bounded by the clinic's data, as the PRD accepts. The PRD test_names stay in VetControllerTests as the prd-entry places them. findings.description: The `SpecialtyDirectory` contract row packs two unrelated facts into one ambiguous clause: "Specialties sort by name and holders by last name then first name, with identity matching holders and breaking ties." The trailing clause reads as if identity-matching and tie-breaking are the same mechanism, but they are two separate facts (holders are matched to a specialty by id in `SpecialtyDirectory.holds`; the specialty sort breaks name ties by id in `SPECIALTY_ORDER`). As written the sentence is ambiguous to a reader who has not read the source.
findings.fix: Split into two clauses, e.g.: "Specialties sort by name, breaking ties by id; holders sort by last name then first name and are matched to a specialty by id, not by entity equality."
